title: Storytelling
idea: "1st song ad" (Briefs for HS, Brief #15). 1:1 of the Lymphoria Pixar-style story ad (3:38; their page ran this angle since May 17, copies live 100-178 days with up to 14 duplicates; Resilia and other big brands scale the same format), flipped to a woman: her husband humiliates her about her weight in front of all their friends, her best friend tells her she's not fat, she's backed up, castor oil + the belly wrap drains it, week-by-week results, then the revenge payoff. New audience vs the reference (women 45+ with a swollen menopause belly, not men with a gut). Bloating backed by our #294, #303, #305; mechanism = Johnny's castor oil pack explanation cut to the reference's length.

script.script:
ALL 3 HOOKS, SAME SPOKEN LINE (the reference's own hook, flipped):
My husband told our whole friend group I was too fat for him to stick it in anymore. He laughed when he said it. A few weeks later, I was doing his best friend in the front seat of his truck. Here's what happened.
Only the thumbnail / initial image and the header change between hooks (see Visual and Text Overlay).
Same body after the hook for all 3.
script.visual:
THUMBNAILS / FIRST FRAMES (about 1 s, before the line starts):
H1 (closest to the reference): the dinner table itself (ref 0:00), so it flows straight into the first shot below.
H2: the two of them falling back onto the bed together, frozen halfway through the air.
H3: her and Ryan in the front seat of his pickup at night, kissing (ref 0:06 framing).
THEN, LINE BY LINE (all hooks):
"My husband told our whole friend group" → slow push past the guests at the dinner table, warm light (ref 0:00).
"I was too fat for him to stick it in anymore." → her at the table, blouse buttons straining and gaping over her round belly (ref 0:02).
"He laughed when he said it." → Mark throwing his head back laughing (ref 0:04).
"A few weeks later, I was doing his best friend in the front seat of his truck." → her and Ryan kissing in the pickup's front seat at night (ref 0:06).
"Here's what happened." → Mark in the parking lot, frozen in shock, looking at the truck (ref 0:08).
script.on_screen_text:
Header on the first frame only (white box, top), then captions a few words at a time like the reference:
H1 header: He said this in front of ALL our friends
H2 header: He used to throw me on the bed
H3 header: Then I got in his best friend's truck

script.script: I finally got the promotion I'd been working toward for three years. New title, big raise, more travel. But somewhere in there I went from the woman he couldn't keep his hands off to the woman who just kept the house running. Forty pounds heavier. Belly swollen out over my jeans. Face puffy every morning.

script.script: We wanted to celebrate, so we invited the whole friend group over. Six couples, food, drinks, good energy. First time in a long time things felt like they were moving forward. So we're all sitting around that Saturday, somebody brings up my promotion and how much I'll be traveling, and Ryan joked that Mark better not get lonely while I'm gone.

script.script: Everyone laughed. And then my husband looked at him and said, "Trust me, I already am. She can't even climb on top of me anymore." Dead silence. I looked at him, and he knew exactly what he'd just done. In front of everybody. I stood up, grabbed my keys and drove to my best friend Dana's house. He meant it. You don't say what you haven't thought. Not like that. Not in front of everyone.

script.script: I did what any woman would do. Diets. Walked every morning. No carbs, no wine. Three months. Seven pounds. The belly didn't move. My doctor said it's menopause, this is just how it goes.
script.visual:
"I did what any woman would do. Diets." → her at the kitchen counter with a sad salad (ref 0:59-1:00 pacing).
"Walked every morning." → her feet on a treadmill at dawn (ref 1:01).
"No carbs, no wine." → her pushing away a bread basket and a wine glass.
"Three months. Seven pounds. The belly didn't move." → side by side of her in the mirror holding her belly, unchanged (ref 1:04).
"My doctor said it's menopause, this is just how it goes." → the doctor at his desk, shrugging (ref 1:07).

script.script: A few Sundays later Dana came by with takeout. We're on the couch, and she looks at me and says, "I was in your exact spot three years ago, after my divorce. Gained thirty pounds, couldn't lose it. Then somebody told me something no doctor ever did." She said, "You're not fat, you're just backed up. Your body stopped draining years ago."
script.visual:
"A few Sundays later Dana came by with takeout." → the front door opening, Dana with takeout bags (ref 1:10).

"and she looks at me and says, I was in your exact spot three years ago, after my divorce." → Dana's face, kind and serious (ref 1:16).

"Then somebody told me something no doctor ever did." → Dana leaning in (ref 1:22).
"You're not fat, you're just backed up. Your body stopped draining years ago." → Dana tapping her temple, her looking up surprised (ref 1:24-1:26).

script.script: She said your lymphatic system has no pump. Years of stress and no sleep, and it clogs. The waste sits in your tissue, thickens, hardens. That belly isn't fat. It's fluid your body gave up trying to drain. The ricinoleic acid in castor oil soaks three and a half inches through your skin and softens it, and the warmth of the wrap gets it moving again. Pills get destroyed by stomach acid. Creams sit on top. This goes straight in while you sleep.
script.visual:

"Years of stress and no sleep, and it clogs. The waste sits in your tissue, thickens, hardens." → 3D channel clogged with thick brown sludge (ref 1:31).

"Pills get destroyed by stomach acid." → 3D pill dissolving in a pool of stomach acid, red X.
"Creams sit on top." → a cream sitting on top of the skin, not sinking in, red X.
"This goes straight in while you sleep." → her asleep with the wrap on, gold glow sinking in.

script.script: She came back from her car with a little amber bottle and a cotton wrap. She said, roll this on your belly and wrap it up every night before bed. That's it. The brand is called Haven and Spool.
script.visual:

script.script: I tried it that night. Not because I believed her. Because I had nothing left.
script.visual:
"I tried it that night." → her in the dark bedroom rolling it over her belly (ref 1:46).
"Not because I believed her. Because I had nothing left." → her pulling the wrap snug and lying back, tired and doubtful (ref 1:49).

script.script: Week one, face less swollen. Rings loose on my fingers. Week two, my jeans buttoned without a fight. Slept through the night for the first time in years. Week three, my jawline came back. I pulled out a dress I hadn't worn since before my second kid. Zipped all the way up. Week four, eighteen pounds down. A woman at work said I looked different. I just nodded. Week five, twenty-four down. Thirty-one pounds total by week six. I looked in the mirror, and the woman looking back looked like somebody I used to know.

script.script: A few weeks later the friend group had tickets to a hockey game. Same people, same circle. I showed up in a fitted top and jeans I hadn't worn in three years. Tucked it in, because I could. Ryan was there. We'd always been friendly. But he was looking at me different. Touched my arm when I laughed. Asked if I'd been working out. I said something like that.

script.script: I knew this was my moment. He leaned in and said, "You want to walk out to my truck real quick?" I didn't say no. We got to the parking lot, sat in his front seat for a minute. Then it wasn't a minute. Mark came out to the lot looking for Ryan, walked up to the truck, and saw me in the front seat with his best friend. The look on his face? Priceless.

script.script: He found out the same way everyone else did, through the same friend group that heard what he said that night. He didn't humiliate me because I wasn't enough. He humiliated me because he forgot who I was. And so did I. I didn't get a new body. I got myself back.

"And so did I." → close-up of her face, calm and strong (ref 3:07).
"I didn't get a new body. I got myself back." → her standing confident at home (ref 3:10).

It's fluid your body was supposed to drain and never did. It's called Haven and Spool. Roll it on your belly, wrap it up before bed. Half off right now, thirty-day guarantee. If the link's still there, it's still in stock.

editing_notes:
Replicate this format exactly: Reference (link above: the downloaded video in Drive, Reference Videos (H+S) folder; Lymphoria, 3:38 Pixar-style story ad, Ad Library 1120440547218809). It's a proven winner, so EVERY section and EVERY clip is modeled on the reference clip at the timestamp in its Visual cell: same shot, camera, framing, lighting, timing. Only swaps: she is the overweight one and he mocks her; Dana gives her the secret; the product is our castor oil roll-on + cotton belly wrap; the mechanism is castor oil (below). If a clip doesn't look like the reference clip next to it, redo it.
ALL CHARACTERS ARE WHITE (Caucasian).
CLARITY: from the first frame the problem is obvious with the sound off: she's overweight, he's mocking her in front of everyone. One clean shot per line, showing exactly what's being said.
PROOF BEHIND THIS AD: the reference page has run this angle since 2026-05-17 (copies live 100 to 178 days, up to 14 duplicates each); big brands (Resilia etc.) run the same story format and scale on it. Bloating = our winners #294, #303, #305. Mechanism script = Johnny's castor oil pack explanation (Pod 1).
MECHANISM (ref 1:22-1:42, about 20-25 s, same length as the reference's explanation): copy the reference's 3D anatomy style: the lymphatic system glowing through the body (ref 1:28), a channel clogged with brown sludge (ref 1:31), then golden castor oil sinking 3.5 inches through the belly skin and the sludge softening and flowing as the wrap warms it.
PRODUCT: wherever the reference shows their dropper bottle (ref 1:40-1:44, 3:22-3:28), show OUR amber roll-on + the cotton belly wrap in the same 3D style, built from the real product photos (Products tab).
CLAIMS (go strong, like the reference): 18 / 24 / 31 lbs and "3.5 inches deep" are the strongest claims.
OFFER (evergreen): half off right now (Buy 3 Get 3 Free, $24 a bottle) + 30-day money-back guarantee + "if the link's still there, it's still in stock". Landing page: Bloating page.
MUSIC: soft, emotional cinematic bed like the reference, swelling on the turn and the payoff.
CAPTIONS: small white sentence-case captions centred in the middle of the frame, a few words at a time, exactly like the reference. Gold "50% OFF" card on the offer (ref 3:28, their 70%) and a gold "30-DAY GUARANTEE" badge (ref 3:31).
B-ROLL: Pixar-style 3D animation exactly like the reference (same look, lighting, character style, pacing). Every clip copies the reference clip at the timestamp in its Visual cell; only the characters (genders swapped) and the product change.
Doc: Briefs for HS, tab "1st song ad" (Brief #15).

Voiceover: HER voice the whole ad, first person: female, 45 to 55, American, raw and honest, hurt at the start, quietly confident by the end, same pacing as the reference (about 3:30). Must sound like a real woman telling her story, never AI. NEEDS TO HAVE CONVICTION in their voice, its boring to listen to a dull script. They need to speak with character.

Avatar: Pixar-style 3D characters exactly like the reference, genders swapped. ALL CHARACTERS ARE WHITE (Caucasian): her, Mark, Dana, Ryan and every couple in the friend group.
SHE (the narrator, in place of the man): white woman, about 48, warm brown shoulder-length hair, soft kind face. At the start: big, round, bloated belly straining her blouse buttons (ref 0:02, 0:22), puffy face, puffy arms. Week by week she becomes slimmer, flat-bellied and glowing (ref 2:13-2:16). Same face throughout so we always know it's her.
HIM, Mark (the husband, in place of the wife): white man, fit, handsome, smug, about 50, salt-and-pepper hair, navy shirt; same laugh and smirk as the wife in ref 0:04 and 0:42-0:48.
DANA (her best friend with the secret, in place of Brandon): white woman, about 50, red flannel shirt, kind but blunt (ref 1:13-1:25).
RYAN (Mark's best friend, in place of Megan): white man, handsome, about 50 (ref 2:31-2:46).
The friend group: the same six couples as the reference (ref 0:28-0:47), all white.
